pool.text: Founded as the Fort of São José do Rio Negro in Manaus.
Elevated to town status and named Manaus.
Governor Herculano Ferreira Pena restored the name "Manaus".
Mercado Adolpho Lisboa opened, becoming the oldest marketplace in Manaus.
Amazonas Opera House inaugurated with 700 seats and European materials.
Federal University of Amazonas founded, Brazil's oldest federal university.
Sul América Esporte Clube founded, later winning two state titles.
Adolfo Ducke Forest Reserve established, covering 100 square kilometres.
Vivaldão stadium inaugurated, later replaced by Arena Amazônia.
Area created as ecological interest zone within Manaus.
Rio Negro State Park South Section established, protecting 86,601 hectares.
Rio Negro Left Bank Environmental Protection Area created, covering 75% of the bank.
Opera house reopened for live performances after a 90‑year gap.
Third cargo terminal at Manaus airport opened on December 14.
Bilhares Park established in the Planalto neighborhood.
Tupé Sustainable Development Reserve created 25 km west of the city.
TAM Airlines inaugurated its own cargo terminal near Manaus airport.
Massive prison riot began in Manaus and spread to other cities.
COVID‑19 Lineage B.1.1.248 variant outbreak started in Manaus.
Estimated population reaches 2,279,686 across 11,401 km².
